purpose: Recover the four harmonisation columns the seed review omits (collection year, mcr variant, detection method, sampling design) from the primary papers behind the six largest rows and the two self-contradicting rows of research/mcr-colistin-seed.json, so the sector pattern can be re-read with its confounders. Hand-read from the stored Europe PMC records; the numeric cross-checks are pinned in tests/test_mcr_primary_studies.py.

papers.citation: Liu Y-Y, Wang Y, Walsh TR, et al. Lancet Infect Dis 2016;16(2):161-168.
papers.mcr_variants: mcr-1 (the first description of any plasmid-mediated colistin resistance)
papers.detection_method: Whole-plasmid sequencing and subcloning to identify the gene; conjugation and a murine thigh model for mechanism. The prevalence-screening method is NOT stated in the abstract.
papers.sampling_design: Routine antimicrobial-resistance surveillance on commensal E. coli from food animals; isolate/sample-based, but the denominator sums three different sampling units: 523 raw-meat samples, 804 animals, and 1322 inpatient samples from five provinces.
papers.verdict: Arithmetic faithful to the primary (78+166+16=260; 523+804+1322=2649). The confounder is the unit: the seed's single 'Raw meat, livestock, and human' numerator sums three non-comparable sampling frames.

papers.citation: Chen X, Zhao X, Che J, et al. J Med Microbiol 2017;66(2):119-125.
papers.collection_years: NOT stated in the abstract (samples from 20 provinces and municipal cities)
papers.detection_method: Real-time PCR, an assay established in this study, applied to isolates and to faecal samples.
papers.sampling_design: Isolate-based screening of 2330 isolates (10 species) from 20 provinces, plus a SEPARATE faecal arm of 337 samples (229 human, 108 pet). The seed uses only the isolate arm.
papers.denominator_unit: isolates (the faecal arm is a separate denominator and is correctly excluded from the seed row)
papers.verdict: Arithmetic faithful to the primary (2330 isolates, 54 = 2.3% mcr-1). Confounder: the same paper's faecal arm found 14 positives (6 human, 8 pet) on a different denominator; the seed's single row cannot express that.

papers.citation: Kawanishi M, Abo H, Ozawa M, et al. Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2017;61(1):e02057-16.
papers.collection_years: NOT stated in the abstract or the available front matter (brief report; samples from the JVARM monitoring programme)
papers.detection_method: Gene screening for mcr-1 and mcr-2, plus a sequence-homology search of the study's curated GenEpid-J database for mcr-2.
papers.sampling_design: Isolate-based screening of 9306 E. coli from healthy food-producing animals (cattle, swine, broilers) under the Japanese Veterinary Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring (JVARM) system -- routine national surveillance of healthy animals.
papers.verdict: Arithmetic faithful to the primary (9306 screened, 39 mcr-1). Confounder: a healthy-animal national monitoring denominator, not a clinical one; the collection period is not recoverable from the open record.

papers.citation: Ewers C, Gopel L, Prenger-Berninghoff E, Semmler T, Kerner K, Bauerfeind R. Front Microbiol 2022;13:1076315.
papers.mcr_variants: mcr-1 and mcr-2 (including a new allele mcr-2.8)
papers.detection_method: Archived isolates were stored only if positive for a virulence-associated gene (STEC/ETEC/EPEC) and then screened for mcr-1/mcr-2 with genomic characterization (WGS, plasmid typing); the second arm used sheep blood agar containing 4 mg/L colistin (selective culture).
papers.sampling_design: TWO sampling frames in one paper: (a) 7614 archived porcine E. coli from faecal samples, 2010-2017, stored only when virulence-gene positive -- a selected archive, not a random sample; (b) 1477 E. coli from colistin-selective agar, 2018-2020 -- a colistin-enriched denominator.
papers.verdict: SEED DEFECT RESOLVED against the primary. Primary Table 1: Germany 6158 isolates, mcr-1 = 707 (11.5%). The seed prints n=709 and 10.42%; 10.42% is the STUDY-WIDE total (793/7614 = 10.4%), not Germany's rate, and 707 vs 709 is a 2-isolate difference.

papers.citation: Ewers C, et al. Front Microbiol 2022;13:1076315 (same paper as row 17a).
papers.collection_years: 2010-2017 (the arm that carries the per-country rows)
papers.sampling_design: Per-country sub-rows of the Ewers 2010-2017 European porcine collection (the seed split one paper into eleven country rows).
papers.verdict: SEED DEFECT RESOLVED against the primary. Primary Table 1: Spain 28 isolates, mcr-1 = 16 (57.1%); Portugal 28 isolates, mcr-1 = 17 (60.7%). The two are NOT identical. The seed duplicated Portugal's row (28/17/60.7) into Spain; Spain should be 28/16/57.1.

papers.citation: Treilles M, Chatre P, Drapeau A, Madec JY, Haenni M. Front Microbiol 2022;13:1023403.
papers.collection_years: 2018-2019 (from the full text; NOT stated in the abstract)
papers.mcr_variants: mcr-1 (specifically mcr-1.1) only; mcr-2 to mcr-5 and mcr-9 were looked for and not found
papers.detection_method: Colistin-resistant isolate screening, then mcr-1 to mcr-5/mcr-9 screening; MLVA PCR typing; Southern blot with short-read and long-read sequencing to localize the gene (chromosome vs IncX4/IncHI2 plasmids).
papers.sampling_design: Farm survey: 80 goat breeding farms (10 adults + 10 kids each) plus 5 fattening batches; 1561 animals (breeding) + 140 (fattening) = 1701 animals, sampled across two production stages.
papers.denominator_unit: animals (the seed's column labels it isolates)
papers.verdict: SEED DEFECT RESOLVED against the primary. Primary: 65/1561 breeding and 84/140 fattening = 149 mcr-1-positive of 1701 animals. The seed prints n=49 -- 149 with the leading digit dropped -- and labels the denominator isolates when it is animals, so the seed's 2.88% is wrong twice. Design confounder: 4.2% vs 60.0% by production stage.

papers.citation: Walkty A, Karlowsky JA, Adam HJ, et al. CMAJ Open 2016;4(4):E641-E645.
papers.detection_method: CLSI broth microdilution for colistin susceptibility, with mcr-1 PCR applied ONLY to the colistin-resistant subset (a screening cascade).
papers.sampling_design: Isolate-based national surveillance (CANWARD): consecutive clinical isolates, one per patient per infection site, from blood, respiratory, urine and wound infections at 10-15 sentinel hospitals.
papers.verdict: Arithmetic faithful to the primary (5571 isolates; 12 colistin-resistant; 2 mcr-1-positive). Confounder: the numerator is a subset of a subset -- mcr-1 was tested only among the 12 colistin-resistant isolates, so the 0.04% is mcr-1 among colistin-resistant isolates, not among all isolates.

ewers_table1.source: Ewers et al. 2022, Front Microbiol 13:1076315, Table 1 (full text, PMC9780603)

divergences.note: the seed's 709 differs from the primary's 707 by 2 isolates
the seed printed the study-wide total (793/7614 = 10.4%) in a country sub-row; the primary's Germany rate is 11.5%
the seed duplicated Portugal's row; the primary's Spain rate is 57.1%, Portugal's is 60.7%
the seed merged mcr-1 (11) and mcr-2 (9) into one numerator; the primary prints them separately
the primary prints 65 (breeding) + 84 (fattening) = 149 mcr-1-positive; the seed's 49 drops the leading digit
the seed labels 1701 as isolates; the primary's 1701 are animals

coverage.note: of the four harmonisation columns the seed omits, over the six distinct primary papers (rows 1, 6, 13, 17a, 19, 28)
